Theorem
[sectional-curvature pinching implies closeness to constant curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0450 ↗ thm:pet-ch11-ricci-pinching-einstein-closeness ↗ lem:pet-ch11-cheeger-injectivity-radius-lemma 1. ch11:11.4.17For $n\ge 2$, $v,D>0$, and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}$, there is $\varepsilon (n,\lambda ,D,v)>0$ such that any closed Riemannian $n$-manifold $(M,g)$ with $\diam \le D$, $\vol \ge v$, $|\sec -\lambda |\le \varepsilon $ is $C^{1,\alpha }$ close to a metric of constant curvature $\lambda $.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch11-sec-pinching-constant-curvature-closeness \sketch By subsection 4.3, curvature, diameter, and volume bounds give a uniform injectivity radius; subsection 4.5 then gives an Einstein limit with $\Ric =(n-1)\lambda g$. In polar coordinates, Hessian comparison for $\lambda -\varepsilon _i\le \sec _{g_i}\le \lambda +\varepsilon _i$ passes to

\[ \Hess r=\frac{\mathrm{sn}_{\lambda }^{\prime }(r)}{\mathrm{sn}_{\lambda }(r)}g_r. \]

The equality case forces constant sectional curvature $\lambda $.

□
